about: Negative controls for the witness branch. Expected values are what each implementation DID on 2026-10-12, not what it should do: a row labelled requirement whose verify_py value contradicts its spec note is a pinned known divergence, so the runner stays green until someone changes behaviour on purpose and updates this file in the same commit.

observed.reference: 1f916-ai/protocol verify.mjs @ 890f4f9 and @ 728e33e (verify.mjs identical), and PR #16 head 422fa78b08f58c6d6436cd7d5b7bdc230ee89274, node 20.19.2

labels.requirement: spec text fixes the verdict (section cited)
labels.choice: spec is silent; each implementation's choice is pinned
labels.proposed-requirement: one reading of the spec fixes it, another does not; contested

credits: rows 2-5 are tally-stick's (c100357) and were first run on both implementations by Jaybob (#8324, on the 09-15 commonwealth fixture); the label split follows ning-qinghan (c103270) and Jaybob (c103454).

rows.name: witness_public_key-flipped
rows.mutation: matching line's witness_public_key changed by one char; --witness-key still pinned
rows.label: proposed-requirement
rows.spec_note: SPEC §8 lists 'a key does not match a pin' under diverged. tally-stick (c100357, #8269) read this as spec-silent; I read §8 as covering it. Contested until someone with the spec says which.

rows.name: status-refused-registry-key-epoch
rows.label: requirement
rows.spec_note: SPEC §6 NORMATIVE (2): a refusal line MUST fail the run

rows.name: registry-field-deleted
rows.label: choice
rows.spec_note: Spec silent on the label. Reference @890f4f9 skips the line (witness-unusable); protocol PR #16 @422fa78 verifies under the caller's origin (witnessed), matching verify.py (Jaybob #8324, tally-stick c101614).

rows.name: consistency-first-observation
rows.mutation: consistency changed from 'verified from 19545' to 'first observation'
rows.label: requirement
rows.spec_note: SPEC §6 NORMATIVE (1): a verifier MUST NOT grant its top verdict to a countersignature whose continuity the witness did not prove. verify.py grants witnessed: this row is expected to FAIL until verify.py reads the consistency field.

rows.name: root-hex-flipped
rows.mutation: matching line's root changed by one hex char (its signature no longer verifies)
rows.label: choice
rows.spec_note: Reference: 'witness copy DISAGREES' -> diverged. verify.py matches lines on root too, so the line is not found -> witness-unusable. Both exit 1. SPEC §8 diverged covers 'a witnessed head conflicts', but this line's signature does not verify, so whether it is a witnessed head is open.

rows.name: status-pending
rows.mutation: status changed from countersigned to pending (signature still valid)
rows.label: choice
rows.spec_note: Reference counts only status=countersigned as a countersignature (consistent-unwitnessed); verify.py ignores status except refusal words (witnessed). Spec does not define the status vocabulary beyond refusals.

rows.name: matching-line-deleted
rows.label: requirement
rows.spec_note: SPEC §8 witness-unusable (both agree on the verdict). SPEC §8 also says implementations SHOULD make its exit status distinct: reference exits 3, verify.py exits 1, the same code as diverged.
